newsitem.title: USA: U.S. help-wanted ad index rose to 90 in February.
newsitem.headline: U.S. help-wanted ad index rose to 90 in February.

text.p: The U.S. help-wanted advertising index rose three points to 90 in February from 87 in January, the Conference Board said on Thursday.
"The job market continues to show surprising strength," said Conference Board economist Ken Goldstein.
He said a pickup in employment mixed with slowing job cuts suggests the labor market "is about to become even tighter."
Goldstein said that job growth is "unlikely to slow to an average of 200,000 new jobs per month, even with a new and more restrictive monetary policy in place."
Consumer confidence has derived some strength from dominant trends in the labor market, such as sustained job growth and slight advances in hourly compensation, Goldstein added.

In the last three months, the volume of help-wanted advertising rose in six of the nine U.S. regions. The greatest increase was in the Middle Atlantic region, up 16 percent. Other regional increases were in the Pacific, up 6.8 percent, East North Central, up 3.5 percent and South Atlantic, up 3.2 percent.
Regional declines were in New England, down 9.8 percent, East South Central, down 2.2 percent and Mountain, down 2.5 percent.
